# Feature Maturity

Not every feature in ferx-core is equally battle-tested. Some — like FOCE/FOCEI
estimation and the analytical PK solutions — have been validated against gold
standard engines across many datasets. Others are newer and have only been
exercised on a handful of examples. To make this explicit, every major feature
carries a **maturity label**.

Where a feature has its own dedicated reference page, that page repeats its label
in a banner at the top, e.g.:

> **Maturity: beta** — see [Feature Maturity](maturity.qmd) for what this means.

The table below is the authoritative list; a few features documented inside a
shared reference page (e.g. the gradient method under [Fit Options](model-file/fit-options.qmd))
or only in an example carry their label here rather than in a per-page banner.

## Maturity levels

| Label | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **stable** | Well-tested functionality with proven stability across diverse datasets and estimation options. Performance is comparable to (or better than) gold standard NLME engines (NONMEM, Monolix). Safe for production use. |
| **beta** | Stable in limited testing and across a range of fit settings, but some caution is warranted before relying on it in production on unseen datasets. Validate against a reference where you can. |
| **experimental** | New functionality tested only on a single example or a small handful of (often toy) examples. Behaviour and syntax may change. Results should be treated as provisional and validated carefully. |

These labels describe ferx-core's *current* state and will move upward as
features accumulate testing and cross-validation. Most of ferx-core is currently
**beta**, with a mature core approaching **stable**; a few features remain
**experimental**.

## Runtime warnings

Two **experimental** features emit a warning at fit time (surfaced in
`FitResult.warnings`, the CLI output, and `ferx check`) so their status is
visible at the point of use. The others are flagged only by their label here and
on their reference page:

| Feature | Warning code |
|---------|--------------|
| Stochastic differential equations (`[diffusion]`) | `W_EXPERIMENTAL_SDE` |
| Neural networks (`[covariate_nn]`) | `W_EXPERIMENTAL_NN` |

**Beta** and **stable** features do not emit a maturity warning.

### Model-based meta-analysis (MBMA) features

The pieces of an MBMA model, in the order [Model-based meta-analysis: start
here](model-file/mbma.qmd) introduces them. Each is labelled **beta** on the
strength of the NONMEM anchor named in its row (catalogued in
`nonmem_anchor/README.md`); the anchors cover single models, not the range of
datasets **stable** asks for.

| Feature | Maturity | Reference | NONMEM anchor |
|---------|----------|-----------|---------------|
| θ level blocks (`theta NAME[LEVEL]`; `sum_to_zero` / `sum_to_zero_within` / contrasts; per-level SEs) | **beta** | [Theta level blocks](model-file/parameters.qmd#theta-level-blocks) | `level_two_block`, `level_se_{a,b}`, `level_no_gaussian` (read by a TTE hazard) |
| `profile`d level blocks (incl. bounded) | **beta** | [Profiled level blocks](model-file/parameters.qmd#profiled-level-blocks) | `profile_mbma`, `profile_mbma_bound`, `profile_mbma_tve0_55`; with a `correlation` line, no NONMEM run: it matches the anchored unprofiled fit ([With a profiled level block](model-file/residual-correlation.qmd#with-a-profiled-level-block)) |
| Nested variability levels (`level … in …`, `kappa … at LEVEL`) | **beta** | [Nested levels](model-file/iov.qmd#nested-levels) | `nested_levels_3` (OFV, EBEs), `nested_levels_3_cov` (R-matrix SEs) |
| Within-arm residual correlation (`cs` / `ar1` / `car1`, incl. with a kappa) | **beta** | [Within-group residual correlation](model-file/residual-correlation.qmd) | `residual_correlation/*` (naproxen, real data); `nested_levels_3_ar1/*` (with kappa) |
| Residual `weight =` and kappa `weight =` | **beta** | [Residual weighting](model-file/error-model.qmd#residual-weighting-weight-...), [Sample-size-weighted IOV](model-file/iov.qmd#sample-size-weighted-iov-weight-...) | `mbma_canakinumab` (both, real data); `residual_correlation/*` (residual); `nested_levels_3` (kappa) |
| Compartment-free (algebraic) `[structural_model]` | **beta** | [Compartment-Free Models](model-file/structural-model.qmd#compartment-free-models-the-pred-equivalent) | `algebraic_emax` vs `$PRED` |

For the MBMA group, a feature's section banner and its row in this table must
agree; when one changes, change the other in the same PR.

> The label reflects the engine's overall confidence in a feature, not the
> presence or absence of tests — a beta feature may still have extensive
> automated tests; "stable" additionally requires broad cross-validation against
> reference engines across diverse datasets.
